# Desktop app: build rules

Apply these rules while you build. Domains or criteria whose `applies_if` flags are false in `.quality/project.json` do not apply to this project. Before you call a task done, check your work against the criteria of the domains you touched: each one must be true and verifiable.

If a stack module of Shipwright is installed (sw-nextjs, sw-node-api, sw-vps, sw-expo, sw-capacitor, sw-tauri, sw-electron), its rules skill adds stack-specific rules on top of these.

## Desktop experience (DUX)

Window, menus, shortcuts, files, offline: what people expect from an app installed on a computer.

Applies when: Installed desktop app (Tauri, Electron).

Rules:

- A desktop app is not a site in a window: it starts fast, works without network for what is local, and follows the system's habits (menus, shortcuts, drag and drop, recent files).
- Window: a minimum size is set, the layout works from the minimum size to full screen, size and position are remembered between launches, including with several displays.
- System shortcuts honoured (save, undo, redo, close, quit, preferences), with Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere; every menu action is also in the interface.
- No lost work: autosave or a warning before closing with changes, recovery after a crash.
- Files: native dialogs to open and save, drag and drop accepted, long paths and accented characters handled, nothing written outside the folders the user chose or the app's data folder.
- Long operations do not freeze the window: progress shown, cancel possible.
- Light and dark theme following the system; display scaling (125 %, 150 %, 200 %) without blur or clipped text.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] DUX-01: Every key task completes in the real window. Check: flows.json played with `sw flows --attach <port>` on the running app (not only in a browser): every flow completed. Say on which system.
- [major] DUX-02: Window usable at every size, state remembered. Check: Minimum size set in the configuration; screenshots at the minimum size and full screen with no clipped content; size and position restored after relaunch.
- [major] DUX-03: System shortcuts and menus honoured. Check: Save, undo, redo, copy, paste, close, quit and preferences answer the system's shortcuts on each target platform; application menu present on macOS.
- [BLOCKER] DUX-04: No work lost on close or after a crash. Check: Close the window with changes: saved, or a warning. Kill the process while editing then relaunch: the work is back or offered.
- [major] DUX-05: Files handled the way the system expects. Check: Native dialogs; drag and drop; a file with an accented or long name, or on another drive, opens; a missing or locked file gives a clear message; nothing written outside the allowed folders.
- [major] DUX-06: Works without network for what is local. Check: Network off: the app starts, local data opens and can be changed, what needs the network says so without blocking the rest.
- [major] DUX-07: Long operations without freezing, with progress and cancel. Check: Run the heaviest operation on real data: the window still answers, progress moves, cancel works.
- [minor] DUX-08: Fast start, system theme and scaling followed. Check: Window usable in under 2 seconds cold; the system's dark theme followed; sharp display at 150 % and 200 %.

## Desktop release and security (DRL)

Isolation between the page and the system, signing, updates, install and uninstall.

Applies when: Installed desktop app (Tauri, Electron).

Rules:

- The page reaches the system only through a short list of named functions (Tauri commands, Electron preload script); each validates its arguments like a server route.
- Tauri: content security policy set, per-window permissions narrowed to the folders, commands and hosts used. Electron: contextIsolation on, nodeIntegration off, sandbox kept, no http page.
- Installers signed (Windows) and notarised (macOS); otherwise the system warns or refuses.
- Updates signed, served over https, verified before install; the user knows which version they have and what changed.
- Secrets in the system keychain, never in clear in a configuration file; no secret in the shipped package.
- User data in the folder the system provides; uninstalling keeps or removes it as announced.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] DRL-01: Isolation between the page and the system in place. Check: desktop-check.json: no failed "must" (content security policy, permissions or API list, remote access, nodeIntegration, contextIsolation, web security, signed https updates, app identifier).
- [major] DRL-02: Signing, updates and narrowed permissions. Check: desktop-check.json: each failed "should" is fixed or justified (Windows and macOS signing, updater, broad permissions, sandbox, preload script).
- [BLOCKER] DRL-03: Every function exposed to the page validates its arguments. Check: Read every Tauri command or preload function: paths restricted to allowed folders (no ".."), sizes bounded, no command built from input and executed.
- [major] DRL-04: Installers accepted by the system on each target platform. Check: Install the released build on a clean machine: no blocking SmartScreen warning on Windows, opens without a workaround on macOS; the app launches and uninstalls cleanly.
- [major] DRL-05: Update tested end to end, version and changes visible. Check: Install the previous version, publish a test release, check the update downloads, verifies and installs; the version number and the changes are shown in the app.
- [major] DRL-06: Secrets in the system keychain, data in the right place. Check: Look for tokens and keys in the app's files after signing in: none in clear. Data lives in the system's application data folder, not next to the executable.
